messages:
mike: Hey team — customer (Acme) seeing intermittent 504s + duplicate downstream side-effects when using our Go SDK. They report same request_id twice in upstream logs. Attaching trimmed logs and a tiny repro.

mike: logs:
[INFO] request_id=abc123 status=504 took=1.2s retry=1
[WARN] request_id=abc123 context canceled after 400ms
[DEBUG] transport: reusing conn, writing body, attempt=2

elaine: thanks — can you paste the SDK version + Go runtime and a minimal repro? also any request body size or streaming body details?

mike: running go1.20, go-sdk v0.9.1. Body is ~3KB JSON. Repro (simplified):
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 300*time.Millisecond)
defer cancel()
req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate", bytes.NewReader(payload))
req = req.WithContext(ctx)
resp, err := httpClient.Do(req) // httpClient uses default transport with MaxIdleConnsPerHost
if err != nil { log.Printf("err=%v", err) }
// SDK has internal retry that calls Do(req) again on network errors
```

raj: likely culprit: non-rewindable request body + our retry logic. When context times out mid-write, our retry path may call httpClient.Do(req) again using the same req.Body which is already drained. Depending on transport behavior this can manifest as an extra write or an empty body, and upstream treats it as duplicate/garbage -> 504s and duplicate state changes.

raj: quick checklist:
- if req.Body isn't rewindable, transport can't resend it automatically. Use req.GetBody or construct req with bytes.Reader so it can be reset.
- don't retry when ctx.Err() != nil (context canceled/deadline) — treat as non-retriable.
- when retrying, clone the request and provide a fresh Body.

sam: short mitigations until a fix: set transport.DisableKeepAlives = true or add header `Connection: close` to force new TCP connection per attempt (costly, but isolates the repro), or ensure http.Transport.GetBody is set. Also try increasing client timeout vs ctx timeout so we don't cancel while header/body still streaming.

sam: also consider tuning http.Transport.ResponseHeaderTimeout and IdleConnTimeout to avoid weird partial writes.

mike: tried adding `DisableKeepAlives = true` and the duplicates stopped in a quick smoke test. Not ideal for perf.

elaine: can you try upgrading to go-sdk v0.9.3? We changed retry behavior in that release to avoid retries on context.Canceled and to clone request bodies more defensively. If that reproduces, we'll escalate to eng-runtime.

mike: will test upgrade and run a targeted load test. Repro steps I'll run and paste here:
1) build minimal binary with payload generator (3KB)
2) run `GOMAXPROCS=1 ./repro --concurrency=8 --timeout-ms=300`
3) watch upstream logs for duplicate request_id

raj: if you can reproduce, capture pcap or tcpdump + client goroutine stacks: `sudo pkill -ABRT repro` (or use runtime/pprof) to see where cancels happen. Also add `req.GetBody = func() (io.ReadCloser, error) { return io.NopCloser(bytes.NewReader(payload)), nil }` in the repro to test the GetBody path.

infra-bot: deploy: canary rollback job #456 succeeded; no platform-wide config changes in the last 24h.

mike: thanks. I'll try upgrade first, then GetBody. If still failing, I'll attach pprof and tcpdump here and open a support ticket with customer.

elaine: great. if you need eng help, ping @raj and add a short summary of findings. :thumbsup:

raj: one more note — our SDK historically treated 5xx and network errors as retryable and didn't special-case context cancellations. v0.9.3 adds logic to surface ctx errors to the caller and skip retries. If you can't upgrade, patch in a custom RetryPolicy that checks `if errors.Is(ctx.Err(), context.Canceled) || errors.Is(ctx.Err(), context.DeadlineExceeded) { return DontRetry }`.
